transcript:
Header:
Date/Time: 2025-11-26 16:00 PST
Duration: ~45 minutes
Attendees: Jordan Lee (Redwood AE), Priya Nair (Redwood SE), Alex Martinez (CTO, Veridian), Sasha Kim (Security Lead), Ravi Patel (ML Eng), Maya Lopez (PM)

Summary/Goals (auto): sign off success criteria for POC, agree acceptance tests, define reporting and timeline.

[00:00] Jordan: Hey everyone, thanks for joining, I think we're all here. quick intro, I am Jordan, I'm the AE on this account, with Priya our SE.
[00:09] Alex: Hi Jordan, Alex here, Sasha, Ravi, Maya from Veridian. thanks.
[00:15] Priya: great, i'll kick off with the proposed success criteria doc we put in the share — bear with me if some names come out weird on the transcript —
[00:23] Priya: High level we want three buckets: performance (latency/throughput), cost/governance (cost per token, billing), and quality/regression (accuracy, hallucination rate on clinical prompts).
[00:35] Sasha: yeah security is also a hard requirement, we need VPC or private deployment option, KMS integration and audit logs sent to our SIEM, plus SOC2 evidence.
[00:45] Jordan: noted. for performance we proposed 95th percentile latency under 250 ms for single-turn inference at the target prompt length (avg 120 tokens), and a throughput target of 10 QPS sustained for the pilot window. does that align?
[00:58] Ravi: 250ms 95p is tight but doable, what's the tokenization assumption? our prompts average 110-140 tokens incl. system prompt.
[01:07] Priya: yes that's the distribution we tested in our internal preview. we'll run the baseline with the exact tokens you provide. also we suggested a cost target of less than $0.01 per 1k tokens for pilot accounting, this is more of an ops/governance threshold.
[01:21] Maya: for quality how are you quantifying hallucinations? we need a go/no-go threshold we can validate.
[01:27] Priya: good Q, we typically use an evaluation set you provide with expected outputs and two metrics: exact-match/ROUGE or domain-specific F1 for extraction tasks, plus a hallucination rate as measured by a human adjudicator on a 200-sample subset. proposed threshold: F1 >= 0.88 for extraction tasks and hallucination rate < 2% on adjudicated samples.
[01:46] Alex: That sounds reasonable, maybe F1 0.9 for the critical flows, 0.88 for lower-critical.
[01:53] Sasha: we also need error rate SLOs — like API error <0.5% and availability 99.9% for the duration of the pilot.
[02:01] Jordan: yes, agreed — we'll aim for <0.5% error rate and 99.9% availability on Dedicated or Hosted with SLA during pilot. fallback policies will be documented.
[02:12] Ravi: what about model versions — do we freeze a specific model for the acceptance tests?
[02:16] Priya: we'll freeze to the verified candidate model artifact; Redwood will provide the model hash and inference config. if runtime changes we notify and re-run benchmarks.
[02:25] Jordan: ok, timeline: Week 0 (this week) — sign-off on criteria, share dataset. Week 1 — integration + config, run smoke tests. Week 2 — full benchmark run (latency/throughput/cost) + quality eval. Week 3 — results review and decision. so roughly 3 weeks end-to-end for sign-off.
[02:40] Maya: that's doable for us. can you outline the acceptance tests concretely?
[02:45] Priya: yes. acceptance tests we will run: 1) Latency test: run 10k requests with your prompt distribution, measure p50/p95/p99; pass if p95 < 250ms and p99 < 600ms. 2) Throughput/stability: ramp to 10 QPS sustained for 30 minutes with error <0.5%. 3) Cost validation: run a baseline tokenized run and compute estimated cost per 1k tokens; pass if under agreed threshold. 4) Quality evaluation: run automatic scoring on 5k labeled examples plus human review on 200 samples; pass if F1 >= 0.88/0.9 per flow and hallucination < 2%. 5) Security checks: VPC connectivity test, KMS key validation, audit log delivery to SIEM, and confirmation of retention policy.
[03:29] Alex: For the latency numbers, if we see p95 at 300ms but p50 good, is that an immediate fail?
[03:35] Priya: we treat p95 as a gating metric; if it's slightly over we flag for mitigation steps (quantization profile, batching adjustments). if it stays >300ms after optimizations that's a fail. we can accept a single rerun after tweaks.
[03:47] Ravi: how will you report results — we need raw logs and a summary dashboard.
[03:51] Jordan: we'll deliver: 1) a CSV with per-request latency, tokens, error codes; 2) Redwood console dashboard link with per-route metrics; 3) an executive summary PDF with pass/fail per acceptance test and recommended mitigations. CSV and dashboard are primary artifacts for your SREs.
[04:08] Sasha: retention of logs — how long are logs kept in hosted mode? and do you redact PHI?
[04:13] Priya: by default hosted logs are retained 30 days but for pilot we can set retention per contract; for Veridian we'll propose a config: log forwarding to your S3 and then Redwood can set ephemeral retention. PHI must be excluded — customer should sanitize or we can do on-the-fly redaction with caveats. we'll include guidance in the security pack.
[04:33] Alex: what's the acceptance criteria for encryption? we need in-transit plus at-rest with customer KMS.
[04:39] Jordan: accepted — KMS integration (customer-managed keys) for Dedicated and private control plane; we'll show KMS handshake and envelope encryption in the security doc.
[04:47] Maya: on reporting cadence — can we get a daily benchmark summary during the full run and a consolidated report at the end?
[04:53] Priya: yes, we'll provide daily CSV snapshots and a consolidated report with trend charts.
[04:58] Jordan: on cost, just to be super explicit — the pilot estimate is to help you budget; final per-token unit economics are negotiated on commit. for the POC we'll track realized cost and compare to target.
[05:08] Sasha: any competitors we should be aware of here in performance? we've run quick tests with Bedrock and saw varying p95s.
[05:14] Priya: we included some comparative notes in the doc — but the main point is we can run the same benchmark in your environment.
[05:20] Alex: ok i'm comfortable moving forward, how do we sign off formally?
[05:23] Jordan: two-step sign off: 1) this call's notes + acceptance criteria doc signed by Maya/CTO; 2) after benchmark run we produce the acceptance report and you sign final go/no-go.
[05:33] Maya: i'll take the doc and run it by legal and security; Sasha will validate the security items.
[05:38] Sasha: quick item — we will need a redacted SOC2 or equivalent; Jordan you'll send?
[05:42] Jordan: yes I'll attach our SOC2 type II report and the security pack in the next email.
[05:45] Priya: and to reiterate for benchmarks we need the sample prompts + expected outputs, and a staging endpoint to hit. Ravi, can you own the dataset upload?
[05:52] Ravi: yes i'll upload anonymized prompts to the S3 bucket and share access by Dec 1.
[05:57] Jordan: great, so to recap next steps — Jordan sends docs, Veridian uploads dataset, Priya spins staging, run benchmarks week of Dec 8, and we reconvene for results.
[06:07] Alex: thanks all, looking forward.
[06:09] Jordan: thanks everyone.

Notes on transcript quality: auto transcription had a few mis-hearings (K V cache vs KV cache, some proper nouns), manual check recommended for the final artifacts.
